title: Four steps, in order: the clock is part of the problem
caption: Roughly 8 + 15 + 17 + 5 minutes of a 45-minute slot. Each step feeds the next one.

steps.text: Scope (5–8 min): features in and out, the non-functional targets, and a quick estimate. Finish with a one-line summary the interviewer agrees with.
High level (10–15 min): API and data model, then decompose into parts, solve each small, and merge them by node id into one diagram that evolves v1 → v2.
Deep dives (15–20 min): two or three hard parts, each with options, a choice and the reason. This is where the hiring signal is.
Wrap-up (3–5 min): first bottleneck at 10×, failure modes, metrics you would alert on, what you would do next.

scenarios.name: Risk: skip scoping
scenarios.summary: Drawing before scoping feels fast, but a missed requirement found at minute 25 forces a redraw and eats the deep dives.

steps.text: Minute 0: start drawing boxes straight away. No features, no targets, no numbers.
Minute 25: "It also needs to work offline" or "100 M users". Half the diagram is wrong.
The redraw eats the deep-dive time: only shallow answers left, which is weak signal.
Mitigation: always spend the 5 minutes and end scoping with a one-line summary the interviewer agrees with.

scenarios.name: Out of time
scenarios.summary: Going deep on one part for 30 minutes leaves no wrap-up: no bottlenecks, failure modes or next steps. Watch the clock and timebox each dive.

steps.text: Scoping and the high-level design go fine by minute 20.
The first deep dive (say, database schema) runs on for 25 minutes.
The interviewer calls time. No second dive, no failure modes, no "what at 10×".
Mitigation: say your plan up front ("two dives, ~8 minutes each") and check the clock between them.

scenarios.name: Interviewer steers
scenarios.summary: If the interviewer pulls you into one part early, follow them: the steps are a default order, not a script.

steps.text: During the high-level design the interviewer asks: "How exactly would ranking work?"
That is a deep-dive request. Park the rest of the diagram and go deep now.
Afterwards, say so: "Let me finish the write path quickly", and keep a few minutes for the wrap-up.
